patch_description: Fundamentally different approach: instead of stochastic single-point hill climbing in full 2D space (26 free coordinates, where each move randomly disturbs the configuration), we exploit the strong geometric prior that good Heilbronn configurations place points on the boundary of a convex curve (known ~n^-3 scaling for points on convex curves, beating interior placements). We parameterize all 13 points by angles on an ellipse (26 params: 13 angles + 2 semi-axes), making the hull area a smooth, cheaply computable function of the same parameters. We then optimize a smooth soft-min (LogSumExp with growing sharpness p) of all 286 triangle areas divided by hull area, using Adam-style finite-difference gradient ascent with a decreasing learning rate. This gives directed, coordinated moves of all points simultaneously, converging far faster than blind random perturbation within the time budget. Multiple deterministic angle seeds (uniform, staggered, perturbed, affine-scaled) with restarts and a final exact-score selection guarantee determinism and robustness.
